notes: The Bay Area Reporter, 5 January 1984 to 26 December 1985: the 104 weekly issues of those years in the Internet Archive collection bayareareporter (GLBT Historical Society scans, identifiers BAR_YYYYMMDD). Method as in the 1982-1983 batch: text and leaves rebuilt from each item's _djvu.xml, read by hand with no reader pass. The numbered-address passages were clustered by address and the clusters holding an event word were read, then the passages around fire, closing, lost-lease and moving words with no number. Kept: a named business or institution opening, moving, closing or being ordered closed at an address on a stated date. Fourteen findings are one event: the Director of Public Health's order of 9 October 1984 closing 14 bathhouses, sex clubs and adult bookstores, whose list of names and addresses the paper printed; each is worded as what happened to the business at that address and names no one. Not kept: owners, managers, bartenders, performers and patrons; obituaries and memorial notices; the people named in the bathhouse litigation; classified and personal advertisements; small shop openings told only by an advertisement; plans with no outcome in these issues (the Coming Home Hospice in the former convent on Diamond Street); places outside San Francisco. A number the story does not print is taken from another issue of the paper and extra.placement_note says which. Not placed at all: the Western Community Money Center Thrift at Castro and 18th, shut by the state on 20 April 1984, whose number the paper does not print.

coverage.remaining: 1986 to 2005 remain: 1,023 issues in the collection, January 1986 to 28 July 2005.
coverage.note: 104 issues; 12,154 numbered-address mentions on EAS streets, 643 windows after the advertisement filter (297 of them rescued for an event word) in 550 address clusters, of which the 256 holding an event word were read, the second half through a tighter filter that drops classified pages and calendar listings; plus 541 event-word passages, of which the 63 with a fire, closing, lost-lease or moving word and no out-of-town or review marker were read. 33 findings written, each quote found again in the issue's text; 7 take their number from another issue. 27 resolved and published on 26 existing pages; no page seeded. Two conflicts stated on their pages (444 Castro, 369 Ellis). 6 unresolved: 3 thin facts held on parcels with no page (900 Stanyan, 2166 Market, 4056 18th) and 3 whose number EAS no longer has (330 Ritch, 114 Eddy, 3244 21st). The 1983 finding printed as 446 Castro is now placed on 444 Castro, where this batch finds the Atlas building under construction.
